title: METL can build continuous sisal oversight in **4** stages that move from acreage mapping to risk alerts and targeted intervention
subtitle: Illustrative operating sequence for a statewide satellite monitoring platform, structured as a management cycle rather than a technical build plan

phases.title: Acreage mapping creates the statewide sisal baseline METL needs before any ongoing oversight begins
phases.body: Build the first statewide layer that shows where sisal sits, how plots are distributed, and which areas require regular review.

phases.title: Condition monitoring turns the acreage baseline into recurring visibility on crop performance across mapped sisal areas
phases.body: Track crop condition over time from the same mapped footprint so METL sees changes in field status continuously, not through periodic field checks.

phases.title: Risk alerting converts condition signals into early warnings that isolate where sisal stress is emerging
phases.body: Flag anomalies and deteriorating zones early so review shifts to priority areas instead of relying on state teams to discover issues in the field.

phases.title: Directed intervention closes the loop by sending action to the highest-priority sisal areas identified by the platform
phases.body: Use mapped acreage, condition trends, and risk flags in one workflow to target inspections, support, and follow-up where intervention is most urgent.
